title: Moroccan Stuffed Butternut Squash
summary: Sweet roasted butternut squash halves are filled with spiced couscous, herbs, and crumbled feta. It’s a comforting vegetarian dinner with warm Moroccan-inspired flavours.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Halve the butternut squash lengthways and scoop out the seeds. Brush the cut sides with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, season with a little salt, and place cut-side down on a baking tray.
Roast for 30 to 35 minutes, until the flesh is tender and the edges are starting to caramelise.

While the squash roasts, rinse the couscous and put it in a bowl with 180 ml boiling water, a pinch of salt, and a drizzle of the remaining olive oil. Cover and leave for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Finely dice the red onion, grate or finely chop the carrot, and mince the garlic. Warm the remaining olive oil in a pan over medium heat, then cook the onion and carrot for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika, ground coriander, cinnamon, chilli, black pepper, and the remaining salt. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the fluffed couscous, raisins, and chopped parsley. Remove from the heat and crumble in half of the feta.
Turn the roasted squash cut-side up and fill the hollows generously with the couscous mixture. Top with the remaining feta and return to the oven for 5 to 10 minutes, until heated through.
Serve hot, with the squash soft and the filling lightly golden on top.
